# S3 — First-class AWS Bedrock provider (native, no gateway) with measured prompt caching

## Context / Problem

rebar has no Bedrock path. Our clients will reach Claude through Bedrock more often than through the direct
Anthropic API, and PR #121's answer — front Bedrock with an OpenAI-compatible gateway — forces every operator
to stand up and accredit a proxy, and gives up prompt caching, the retrying transport, and native structured
output in the process.

## Approach

Register a `bedrock` builder in the provider factory [rebar:7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1] that constructs pydantic-ai's
native `BedrockConverseModel` with a `BedrockProvider`, authenticating through the ambient AWS credential chain
(instance role in production, `AWS_PROFILE`/env locally) — no rebar-managed key. Prompt caching is already selected by the
`prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` capability shipped in story f184, which sets **exactly two** keys —
`bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions`. An earlier draft of this plan named a third
(`bedrock_cache_messages`); that is **rejected** for parity, because the direct-Anthropic path sets only the
matching two and `AnthropicModelSettings.anthropic_cache_messages` is likewise left unset. Enabling message
caching on Bedrock alone would make it cache MORE than Anthropic, which is a new behaviour with its own cost
and TTL profile — a separate decision with its own measurement, not a third key smuggled in here. The parity
bar in story 0d76 is measured against exactly these two keys. Ships as a new `[bedrock]` optional extra
(`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`) so boto3 stays out of the default `[agents]` install; the builder raises a clear
missing-extra error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

**Caching HAS been measured (real AWS, us-east-2, account 5797…98).** The measurement is done; this section
records the results and the decisions they force, so no implementer has to guess. Oracle: the same request twice
with a `cachePoint` after a ~4000-token stable system prefix, reading `cacheReadInputTokens` /
`cacheWriteInputTokens` off the real Converse response.

1. **On-demand model ids are not invokable at all** in this account/region — both
   `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` and the older `anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` return
   `ValidationException: Invocation of model ID … with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request
   with the ID or ARN of an inference profile.` So this story's original on-demand-vs-profile comparison is
   moot: **only inference profiles work**, and rebar's documented default must be one.
2. **A regional inference profile DOES cache.** `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`: attempt 1
   `cache_write=4017, cache_read=0`; attempt 2 `cache_write=0, cache_read=4017`; reproducible across runs (a
   later run hit a still-warm cache, 5-minute TTL). This **refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381** for this
   model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce.
3. **Caching is MODEL-dependent and fails SILENTLY.** `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` and
   `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` both report `cache_read=0` AND `cache_write=0` on both
   attempts, billing the full 4029 input tokens every call — no error, no warning. A controlled same-model
   comparison (`us.` vs `global.`) showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the **model**, not the profile
   prefix. Silent full-price billing is the real hazard here.
4. `us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` with a `cachePoint` hard-fails:
   `AccessDeniedException: You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching.`

**Decision A — the default is `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`**, the verified-caching regional inference
profile. Config accepts any profile id; this is what the docs recommend and what the parity story measures.

**Decision B — rebar must WARN when caching was requested but both counters are zero.** Because failure is
silent, an operator otherwise pays full input price on every call forever with no signal. This mirrors the
existing `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` telemetry guard: observability only, never blocking.

### Decision C — `temperature` is FATAL on Bedrock for some models (found by measurement, not in the original plan)

`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` with `temperature=0` returns **400 `ValidationException: temperature is
deprecated for this model`**; the identical call without it succeeds. Reproduced through pydantic-ai as well:
`BedrockConverseModel` + `BedrockModelSettings(temperature=0.0)` → `ModelHTTPError` 400.

This breaks rebar's gates on Bedrock, not just a corner case: `runner.py` sets `model_settings["temperature"]`
whenever `cfg.temperature`/`req.config.temperature` is set, and the plan-review **Pass-2 verifiers deliberately
send `temperature=0`** so re-verifying a finding does not resample. Critically,
`_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings` exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's `models/anthropic.py`, **not** in
`models/bedrock.py` — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully (warning: "Sampling parameters
['temperature'] are not supported … will be ignored") and the Bedrock path hard-fails.

**Decision: carry it as a capability — but f184's override table must first learn the MODEL NAME.**

An earlier draft of this decision said "add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock
models". That is **not implementable as f184 shipped**, and the gap is worth stating precisely: f184's
`_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates receive only the `ModelProfile`, and `BedrockModelProfile` carries **no per-model
identifier** (verified: no model/name attribute on the profile object). So the only predicate expressible today
is "is this Bedrock-hosted Claude", which would strip `temperature` from `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` too —
the measured-good default — destroying exactly the greedy Pass-2 determinism this decision exists to protect.

So this story adds a SEPARATE, additive table rather than changing f184's contract. f184 is **closed and its
plan-review attestation is signed**, and it defines its override predicates as `Callable[[ModelProfile], bool]`;
widening that signature would silently redefine a shipped, signed contract from a downstream leaf. The rule is
that the parent wins, so f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` and its `_is_claude` predicate are left **exactly** as
shipped.

1. Add `supports_temperature: bool = True` to `ModelCapabilities`.
2. Add a **second, distinct** override table, `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES: dict[str, Mapping[str, object]]`,
   keyed on the **exact** model id, applied AFTER the profile-shaped overrides. The two tables encode genuinely
   different things and are better apart than merged: f184's keys on *capability shape* (what kind of model is
   this), this one keys on *a specific model's API defect* (this exact id rejects a parameter).
3. Keys are **exact-set membership, never prefix matching**. That is both cleaner — only model ids whose
   behaviour has actually been MEASURED get an entry, so the table never speculates — and it preserves f184's
   attested criterion that `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is empty.
4. **`capabilities_for()`'s BODY changes; its public signature does not.** An earlier draft said "no signature
   change is needed anywhere", which misleadingly implied no change at all. To be exact — the shipped body reads
   only `getattr(model_or_model_string, "profile", None)` and, for strings, `partition(":")`; it never touches
   `model_name`. The required edit, stated as control flow so nothing is left to inference:

   - the private helper becomes `_capabilities_from_profile(profile, model_id: str | None)` — a PRIVATE helper,
     so this is not the signed `_REBAR_OVERRIDES`/`capabilities_for` contract f184 attested;
   - **path 1 (model object):** `model_id = getattr(model_or_model_string, "model_name", None)` (verified: a
     `BedrockConverseModel` returns e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), passed alongside the profile;
   - **path 2 (model string):** the id is the value `partition(":")` ALREADY produces — reuse it, do not re-parse;
   - **path 3 (conservative fallback):** no id is available, so no model-id override applies — the conservative
     record is returned unchanged, exactly as today;
   - **ordering inside the helper:** derive the fields from the profile, apply f184's profile-shaped
     `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` first (unchanged, first-match-wins), THEN apply
     `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES.get(model_id, {})` on top, so an exact-id entry wins over a shape-based one.
     A model id absent from the table changes nothing.

   `capabilities_for()`'s own parameter list, and f184's predicate signature, both stay as shipped.
5. `runner.py` omits `temperature` from `model_settings` when the capability is False, logging once at INFO that
   it did and why.

**This is model-id matching, and that is deliberate, not a relapse.** The epic's criterion forbids selecting
*provider behaviour* by matching a *provider-name* string; recording a known per-model API defect is a different
thing, and it is what pydantic-ai itself does — its profile functions dispatch on `model_name`
(`anthropic_model_profile(model_name)`), and upstream's own `anthropic_disallows_sampling_settings` flag exists
for exactly this class of quirk on the Anthropic side.

**Honest limitation: the list will drift** as AWS deprecates sampling parameters on more models, and an
unlisted-but-affected model still hard-fails. Mitigate rather than pretend: when a Bedrock call fails with a 400
naming a sampling parameter, translate it into an actionable error telling the operator which model id to add
(or to unset `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE`). A denylist is chosen over an allowlist because an unknown-but-affected
model then fails LOUDLY, whereas an allowlist would silently drop temperature from an unknown-but-fine model and
let verdicts resample — a quiet correctness risk is worse here than a loud configuration error.

Rejected alternatives: dropping temperature on ALL Bedrock calls (loses Pass-2 greedy determinism on the
measured-good default); catching the 400 and retrying without it (burns a billable, often multi-minute agentic
call and keys on model-specific error text).

Note this also widens f184's signed capability record, which story 343b stamps into the verdict sidecar — doing
it now is cheaper than after that payload shape is signed in the field. It directly de-risks story eb6e (the
production review-bot cutover with no Anthropic fallback), which would otherwise hard-fail on such a model.

**Alternative rejected:** OpenAI-compatible gateway fronting Bedrock (PR #121). No proxy is needed for the
native path, and the gateway path measurably loses caching and native structured output.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` (**new leaf**, mirroring `anthropic_model.py`) — the `bedrock` builder and
  its `BedrockProvider`/`BedrockConverseModel` construction. It does NOT go in `providers.py`: that file is at
  289 LOC against the **300-LOC cap that is an attested criterion of closed story 7468**, so the builder
  would breach a signed criterion. `providers.py` gains only the one-line registry entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — `supports_temperature` on the record plus a NEW exact-id
  `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` table (Decision C). f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicate signature and
  `_is_claude` are left UNCHANGED — that contract is closed and signed. The profile override for Bedrock-hosted Claude and the `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"`
  cache-settings selection are **ALREADY SHIPPED by closed story f184** — verify, do not re-add.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — omit `temperature` when the capability withdraws it. NOTE: this file is at
  EXACTLY the 800-LOC hard cap (task 2682), so this change must be net-neutral or the split lands first.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — Bedrock region + model-id/inference-profile config keys.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[bedrock]` optional extra.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated.
- `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` (new); `tests/live/test_bedrock_cache.py` (new, env-gated).

## Testing

Two tiers, because the mechanism spans a pure construction path and a real external service.

- Unit (construction, mocked boto3 client): the builder produces a `BedrockConverseModel` whose settings carry
  **exactly the two** `bedrock_cache_*` keys the parity decision above fixes —
  `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` — and NOT `bedrock_cache_messages`; a plain on-demand id and an inference-profile ARN both construct; a missing
  `[bedrock]` extra raises `LLMConfigError` naming the install command. Contrast case: an `anthropic` model
  still gets `anthropic_cache_*`, never `bedrock_cache_*`.
- Live canary (env-gated, `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK=1`, skipped in default CI): issue the same cached-prefix request
  twice and assert `usage.cache_read_tokens > 0` on the second — the observable oracle for "caching works".
  Run it for both the on-demand id and the inference-profile ARN and record both results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<claude-id> rebar review-plan <ticket>` completes with a valid structured verdict
      against real Bedrock, output attached as a comment on this ticket
- [x] **MEASURED** — the cache canary result is recorded on this ticket: on-demand ids are not invokable at all
      here; `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` caches (`cache_write=4017` then `cache_read=4017`, reproducible);
      `us.`/`global.` opus-4-5 silently do not cache. rebar documents `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` as the
      default
- [ ] a test asserts rebar WARNS when caching was requested but both cache counters are zero (Decision B),
      since the failure is otherwise silent and bills full input every call
- [ ] a test asserts `temperature` is omitted for a model whose `supports_temperature` capability is False,
      and still sent for one where it is True (Decision C) — the contrast case
- [ ] unit tests pass with no AWS credentials present (boto3 client mocked), proving default CI is unaffected
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still installs without boto3 (`python -c "import boto3"` fails in that env)
- [ ] f184's shipped contract is untouched: `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates still take a single `ModelProfile`
      argument and `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is still empty
- [ ] a test asserts the conservative-fallback path still returns the unchanged conservative record when no
      model id is available (the third path above), so adding the second table cannot alter it
- [ ] a test asserts an exact-id override WINS over a profile-shaped one for the same model (ordering)
- [ ] a test asserts the model-id override can distinguish two Bedrock model ids — `temperature` withdrawn for
      a measured-affected id and RETAINED for `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` — the contrast case that proves
      the widened predicate actually discriminates rather than blanket-stripping
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite (`make test`) pass, evidenced
      by the Gerrit change id and its `Verified +1` vote recorded in a comment on this ticket (this criterion's
      proof is external to the repo, so it is attested rather than code-verifiable)
